title: Lesson 11: Security Architecture: The Sharing Model, OWD, Role Hierarchy, Sharing Rules, and Manual Sharing
description: Who can see a given record? The four record-level controls that answer it: org-wide defaults, the role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing. How they layer, how they only ever open access, and why 'most permissive wins' is the whole game.

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: Who can see a given record? The four record-level controls that answer it: org-wide defaults, the role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing. How they layer, how they only ever open access, and why 'most permissive wins' is the whole game.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: This lesson is the deep dive every architect needs on the four record-level controls: org-wide defaults (OWD), the role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing.
Your integration can write a record to Salesforce, but that says nothing about who can see it.
Object permissions say a user may touch Accounts; the sharing model says which Accounts.
Get the sharing model wrong and the result is either a sales team that can't see its own territory or, worse, a field user who can see everyone's compensation.
questions.explanation: Your integration can write a record to Salesforce, but that says nothing about who can see it.

questions.question: Which conclusion does the lesson support?
options: A role is "a level of data access that a user or group of users needs." You build branches to model who must see whose data, not to mirror the reporting structure exactly.
